title: Build an IB Geography Study Group That Works
summary: Build an IB Geography study group that stays focused from September to November with clear roles, weekly agendas, case-study practice, and accountability.
body_markdown:
An effective **IB Geography study group** is small, structured, and focused on active practice. Aim for **3-5 reliable members** , meet weekly for 60-90 minutes, and complete individual preparation beforehand. Sessions should test recall, challenge explanations, apply case studies, practise geographic skills, and improve exam responses.


September to November is a useful period for establishing this routine. The group can consolidate new content, build accurate case-study evidence, and identify weaknesses before winter assessments or mock examinations.


### Confirm the syllabus and set goals


First, confirm which Geography course your school follows. IB Geography is in a curriculum transition: students following the course first assessed in 2019 may have different requirements from those studying the revised course introduced for first teaching in 2025 and first assessment in May 2027.


Check your teacher's course outline against the[official IB Geography page](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/geography/) and[IB curriculum updates](https://ibo.org/university-admission/latest-curriculum-updates/) . Resources for another cohort may not match your content or assessment structure.


Set three measurable goals, such as:


- Consolidate topics within two weeks of classroom teaching.
- Complete and review one timed response each week.
- Build verified case-study files with usable evidence.
- Identify personal weaknesses before November assessments.


### Choose reliable members and rules


Friendship alone does not create a productive group. Choose students who attend consistently, prepare independently, and accept constructive criticism. **Three or four students** is usually ideal; five can work with careful timekeeping.


Agree that meetings start on time, agendas are shared 24 hours in advance, and everyone attempts questions independently before discussion. Claims and statistics should have identifiable sources. Phones should only be used for a defined task, and missed preparation should be completed outside the meeting.


### Use a September-to-November plan


The plan should move from organisation to exam application while following your teacher's sequence.


Period Main purpose Useful output


September Establish routines and diagnose gaps Syllabus tracker, baseline quiz, case-study template


October Consolidate and apply content Data-response tasks, diagrams, case-study comparisons


November Increase timed practice and evaluation Timed essays, error log, personal revision priorities


Students following the earlier course can consult the IB[Geography subject brief](https://ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/geography-sl-hl-2017-en.pdf) , but everyone should use the version confirmed by their teacher.


During October, apply content to unfamiliar maps, graphs, photographs, and infographics. In November, reduce summary-making and increase timed responses. The IB publishes[sample examination papers](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/sample-exam-papers/) , while the[RevisionDojo Geography Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-geography/questionbank) supports topic-based practice.


### Follow a consistent meeting structure


A repeated format limits wasted time and makes preparation predictable.


Time Activity Purpose


0-10 minutes Closed-book retrieval quiz Test independent recall


10-25 minutes Explain and challenge Correct misconceptions


25-45 minutes Case study or geographic skill Apply content to evidence


45-70 minutes Individual exam question Practise under time pressure


70-85 minutes Mark and discuss Compare reasoning with criteria


85-90 minutes Assign actions Record what each member must improve


Retrieval should precede discussion. Constructing an answer collectively can make recognition feel like understanding. Research on[collaborative retrieval practice](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10929687/) indicates that collaborative recall can support later individual memory, but every student still needs independent retrieval.


Rotate the roles of **chair** , **timekeeper** , **question leader** , and **evidence checker** . The evidence checker verifies locations, dates, statistics, and sources. Rotation prevents one confident member from becoming the group's permanent teacher.


### Make activities Geography-specific


Geography assessment involves knowledge, application, analysis, evaluation, and geographic skills. Activities should therefore move beyond memorising definitions.


Use a common case-study template containing:


- Location, scale, and date
- Process, issue, causes, and stakeholders
- Impacts, patterns, and management
- **2-4 memorable pieces of evidence**
- Limitations or contrasting perspectives


Practise adapting each example to different command terms. An “explain” response needs causal links, while “evaluate” requires criteria, limitations, and a justified judgement. RevisionDojo's guide to[manageable Geography case studies](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/easiest-geography-case-studies-for-ib-exams) and the[IB Geography resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-geography) can support this work.


For skills practice, interpret the same unfamiliar stimulus silently before comparing patterns, anomalies, relationships, scale, and limitations. For essays, use a plan, write, challenge, and rewrite cycle instead of producing one shared answer.


### Give feedback that improves answers


Peer marking is useful only when it refers to the question, command term, and available assessment criteria. Start by asking the writer to identify the response's main claim and strongest evidence. The reviewer should then locate one successful feature, one precise weakness, and one revision that would raise the mark. General comments such as “add detail” are less helpful than instructions such as “explain how this statistic supports your judgement about scale.”


When a markscheme is available, use it to understand acceptable answers rather than to copy wording. Geography responses can earn credit through valid reasoning or evidence not listed in an indicative markscheme, so members should not reject a sound point merely because its example differs. If disagreement remains, flag the issue for the teacher instead of turning confidence into authority.


End feedback with immediate action. The writer should improve a sentence, redraw the diagram, or add a qualified judgement while the reasoning is still fresh. Save one before-and-after example from each meeting. By November, these paired responses provide clearer evidence of progress than the number of pages the group has discussed.


### Keep individual accountability


Every session should produce individual work, such as a timed paragraph, annotated graph, essay plan, sketch map, or short-answer response. Record errors under categories including missing knowledge, inaccurate evidence, command-term mistakes, unsupported evaluation, weak stimulus use, and timing.


Maintain both a shared error log and a personal version. The[RevisionDojo Geography self-study guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-geography-resources-self-study) shows how notes, retrieval, questions, and feedback can form a repeating cycle. Jojo AI can clarify difficult concepts or review reasoning, but attempt the task first and verify feedback against teacher guidance and markschemes.


### Avoid common study-group failures


Shared note-making is the most common problem. Attractive slides or copied summaries feel productive but do not reveal what members can recall or apply independently.


Other warning signs include repeated cancellations, unprepared members, unsupported statistics, and one student writing every answer. Do not divide the syllabus so each person learns only one section. Teaching can reinforce understanding, but everyone remains responsible for the complete assessed course.


Coursework must remain each student's own work. Discuss methods or practise with sample data only within teacher guidance, and never copy another member's analysis or wording.


### Review the group in November


At the final November meeting, compare each member's baseline response with a new timed answer and inspect the error log. Continue only if the sessions are improving independent performance.


A productive **IB Geography study group** combines reliable attendance, retrieval, geographic application, and honest feedback. RevisionDojo Study Notes, Flashcards, Jojo AI, the Questionbank, and its[Geography mock-exam guidance](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-geography-mock-exams-for-ib-an-in-depth-guide) can support the next stage of timed practice.
